title: The English Alphabet and Spelling
summary: In this lesson, you will learn the names of the English letters. You will also learn how to spell your name.

sections.p: English has twenty-six letters in the alphabet. There are five vowels (A, E, I, O, U) and twenty-one consonants. Every letter has a special name. When people ask for your name in English, you often need to spell it out loud letter by letter so they can write it down correctly.

ex.en: A, B, C, D, E are the first five letters.

ex.mean: How to say and spell a name.

sections.p: When someone asks 'How do you spell your name?', you say each letter one by one. Listen carefully to the letter names. For example, the letter 'I' sounds like 'eye', and the letter 'Y' sounds like 'why'. Practice saying your name slowly.

ex.mean: The spelling of the name John.

sections.p: In daily life, people often need help with spelling. You can ask someone to repeat the letters if they speak too fast. Polite phrases help you communicate clearly when you meet new friends, check into a hotel, or talk on the phone.

ex.mean: Say it again with more time.

tip: Practice spelling your own name and your friends' names every day. Say the letters out loud to remember their sounds.

quiz.en: There are twenty-six letters in the English ___.
Which of these is a vowel?
When you do not understand, you say: 'Can you ___ that, please?'
